chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hammad ibn Uthman or another, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Fifteen sucklings do not cause prohibition (permanent) prohibition (of marriage). This does not contradict the first report, because the way to reconcile them is to carry it upon the fact that they were separate, in that the suckling of another woman entered between them. For that does not cause prohibition, as clarified in the first report.'

key_terms.الخَبَرَ الأَوّلَ: the first report (referring to a conflicting or complementary hadith)

ai.seo_question: How many breastfeedings are required to establish the prohibition of marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that fifteen breastfeedings establish the prohibition of marriage, reconciling apparent contradictions in hadith by distinguishing between continuous suckling and fragmented instances interrupted by another woman's milk. This nuance reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on contextualizing legal rulings within the broader framework of familial ties (silat al-rahim) and the precise conditions of *radāʿ* (lactation) as derived from the Quran and Sunnah. The ruling underscores the importance of verifying the continuity of nursing events to determine the validity of the mahram relationship in inheritance and marriage law.
